items.name: Amendments Project dataset
items.description: A dataset of the full text of nearly every amendment to the U.S. Constitution proposed in Congress between 1789 and 2022 (more than 11,000 proposals); records of petitions introduced in Congress between 1789 and 1949 that propose, support, or oppose constitutional amendments (more than 9,000 petitions); and thousands of proposed amendments that never made it to Congress. Created by the Amendments Project (PI: Jill Lepore, Department of History, Harvard University; https://amendmentsproject.org) and maintained by Arts and Humanities Research Computing (https://digitalhumanities.fas.harvard.edu/).

items.name: CIM Project Codes for Numerical Simulation
items.description: Monte Carlo simulation of a multimode Coherent Ising Machine (CIM) using quantum jump (MCWF) methods in Python using QuTiP and in Matlab using xSPDE. Features: - Simulates coherent coupling between multiple DOPO modes - Compares vacuum vs coherent superposition initial states - Supports time-dependent parameters - Coupling matrix J determines the Ising Problem - Computes success rate and time/sampling error estimates

items.name: TANDDS project
items.description: The TANDDS(Technological Analysis of Neurodegenerative Disease Using Data Science) project is a research project headed by independent researcher Leah Tibbets. Ms. Tibbets is a Data Scientist and Programmer who has Huntington's Disease, and is especially interested in the application and usefulness of data science in analysis of neurodegenerative disease research data. It is a non-profit charity project whose aim is to help develop better technology to donate to neurodegenerative disease foundations to help in their quest to end diseases like Huntington's Disease, Parkinson's Disease, and Alzheimer's Disease.

items.name: The Combustion Paradox: Socio-Economic and Behavioral Ground-Truth Survey (Purba Medinipur)
items.description: Primary field survey data (n=34) identifying positive deviance, the "Trust Gap", and logistical bottlenecks in crop residue usage across the Kolaghat, Sahid Matangini, and Panskura blocks of West Bengal. This dataset quantifies the prohibitive labor economics (Rs. 600/day baseline), the firewood substitution value of Dhan Siddho (Rs. 4,000-5,200), and the 0% awareness of state-subsidized Custom Hiring Centres among surveyed farmers. It serves as the socio-economic foundation for the Project SATARK AI-logistics architecture.

items.name: The Shift Project
items.description: Using a novel method of online sampling and recruitment, we field surveys to workers at over 150 of the largest companies in retail, food service, grocery, delivery and fulfillment, and hospitality. We provide unique measurement of the reality of working conditions, including not just hourly wages and fringe benefits, but also detailed measures of work scheduling. We pair this in-depth measurement of job quality with detailed measures of financial security and of the health and wellbeing of workers and their families.

items.name: CLIMB Project
items.description: Climate change (interlinked with humanitarian crises and other economic and health factors) could lead to internal resettlements, international migration, and other (new) forms of human mobility. However, the empirical link between various climatic conditions and migration outcomes is highly contested, and, to date, no unified theoretical approach can adequately capture the complexity and contextual dependency of climate-induced migration. To address this gap, CLIMB seeks to develop a holistic approach which will allow us to better understand the mechanisms and pathways underlying the climate-migration nexus, and to predict temporal-spatial mobility patterns in Africa and beyond. Specifically, we will investigate how climate change may intersect with conflicts, poverty, and epidemics, among other adversities, and how these forces may operate in tandem in driving human migration, with a special focus on Africa.
